cgl__tier-2.efficiency_pitch: Tier 2 is 3 marks/Q — massive leverage. Tier A quick-wins: Full Computer module (20 Qs = 60 marks!), Reasoning Analogy+Coding+Series+Mirror+Dice (15 Qs = 45 marks), Science in GA (6 Qs = 18 marks), Simplification+Mensuration 3D (5 Qs = 15 marks), Voice+Speech+Spelling (5 Qs = 15 marks). Combined: ~150 marks for 35-40 study hours. That's 1/3 of total paper marks for a weekend of focused study.

chsl__tier-1.exam: CHSL Tier 1 follows same 4-section × 25-Q structure as CGL Tier 1 but at 10+2 difficulty instead of graduate
chsl__tier-1.efficiency_pitch: Since CHSL is 10+2 level and heavily finite-recall, Tier A topics dominate wins: Science (6 Qs), Culture (1), Geography (2), Mirror/Dice/Fold (4 Reasoning), Coding/Analogy (6 Reasoning), Simplification/Mensuration 3D (4 Quant), Voice/Speech (2 English). That's ~25 Qs = 50 marks for ~20 hours of focused study.

chsl__tier-2.exam: CHSL Tier 2 Session I has both objective + descriptive
chsl__tier-2.efficiency_pitch: CHSL Tier 2 has 3 marks/Q so quick-wins yield big: Coding+Analogy (7 Qs = 21 marks), Mirror+Paper+Dice (6 Qs = 18 marks), Computer module (15 Qs = 45 marks — almost ALL Tier A). ntpc__cbt-2.exam: CBT 2 is the Mains stage for graduate-level NTPC posts; 120 Qs / 120 marks / 90 min
ntpc__cbt-2.efficiency_pitch: NTPC CBT 2 is 1 mark/Q flat — Tier A dominates ROI. Reasoning is almost entirely Tier A (25+ Qs). GA science + culture + sports = 10 Qs easy marks. Mathematics: Simplification + Averages + Mensuration (7 Qs). Railway GK (2 Qs — RRB unique). Combined ~44 marks Tier A for ~25 hours of study. Add Polity (8 Qs / Tier B) for another 8 marks with 10 hrs study. 52 marks / 120 total = 43% — strong CBT-2 qualifying position.
